title: K-flat scalar extension and the affine diagonal module
statement: For a homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ of commutative rings and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define $E_\varphi:D(A)\to D(B)$ by applying the total left derived functor construction to ordinary extension of scalars. This is the K-flat representative model of derived scalar extension [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension]: on a K-flat representative $F$ use $B\otimes_A F$, and on maps use extension of scalars followed by localization. Separately, for commutative rings $R,A$ and an $R$-algebra structure on $A$, put $B=A\otimes_R A$. Define the diagonal object $\Delta_{R,A}$ in $D(B)$ to be the complex concentrated in degree zero with module $A$, restricted from its regular $A$-module structure along multiplication $\mu:B\to A$, $a\otimes a\prime\mapsto aa\prime$. No Noetherian, flatness, finiteness or nonzero hypotheses are part of these definitions.
